 Order

Petitioners are before this Court with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in C.C. No.8801 of 2022 pending before the court of VII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru arising out of Crime No.307 of 2021 registered by Amruthahally Police Station, Bengaluru for offences punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

sentences.text: Accordingly they pray to allow the petition.

4. The copy of memorandum of settlement dated 14th June, 2023 filed in M.C. NO.6708 of 2021 on the file of the III Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru is produced NC:
2024:KHC:10808 CRL.P NO.10382 OF 2023 by the parties before this Court.

entities.text: III Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru

sentences.text:
In Paragraphs 2 and 7 of the said memorandum of settlement, it is stated as follows:
"2. Due to irreconcilable differences and incompatibility of temperaments, the petitioner and respondent have been living separately from 28-6-2021.
the efforts made by the elders, friends and well wishers to resolve the differences between the parties did not yield any fruits.
There is absolutely no chance of reunion between them.
The petitioner and the respondent agree that their marriage is irretrievably broken down and there are no chances of reunion to lead a happy marital life.

Hence,
the petitioner and the respondent have decided to get the marriage between them dissolved by a decree of divorce.
3. xxx
4 . xxx
5 . xxx 6. xxx 7.

In the view of the settlement arrived between the parties, the petitioner has agreed to cooperate with the respondent for the closure/quashing of the criminal case punishable under Section 498-A Indian Penal Code and 3 & 4 of DP Act, in C.C.
No.8801/2022 (FIR No.0254 of 2021) in accordance with law, filed against the respondent and his family members (mother) pending on the file of 7th ACMM,
Bengaluru."
5.

The parties have jointly submitted that, on the basis of memorandum of settlement referred to above, the NC: 2024:KHC:10808 CRL.P NO.10382 OF 2023 jurisdictional Family Court has passed a decree of divorce in M.C. No.6708 of 2021, dissolving the marriage between the parties.
The joint memo is filed by the parties before this Court stating that the respondent No.2 does not intend to pursue the matter as against the petitioners.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of GIAN SINGH vs. STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANOTHER reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303, at paragraph 61 has observed as follows:

entities.text: GIAN SINGH vs. STATE OF PUNJAB AND ANOTHER reported in (2012) 10 SCC 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
"61. The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus:
the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
Sri. Gowtham vs State Of Karnataka By on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45680696/
3

entities.text: Sri. Gowtham vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation but it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power viz; (i) to secure the ends of justice or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

In what cases power to quash the criminal proceeding or complaint or F.I.R may be exercised where the offender and victim have settled their dispute would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case and no category can be prescribed.
However, before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.

Heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, NC: 2024:KHC:10808 CRL.P NO.10382 OF 2023 etc.
cannot be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and the offender have settled the dispute.
Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.

Similarly, any compromise between the victim and offender in relation to the offences under special statutes like Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity etc; cannot provide for any basis for quashing criminal proceedings involving such offences.

But the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and pre-dominatingly civil flavour stand on different footing for the purposes of quashing, particularly the offences arising from commercial, financial, mercantile, civil, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony relating to dowry, etc. or the family disputes where the wrong is basically private or personal in nature and the parties have resolved their entire dispute.

In this category of cases, High Court may quash criminal proceedings if in its view, because of the compromise between the offender and victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of criminal case would put accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by not quashing the criminal case despite full and complete settlement and compromise with the victim.

In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of the criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise NC:
2024:KHC:10808 CRL.P NO.10382 OF 2023 between the victim and wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."
6.

Considering the fact that the dispute between the parties who are close relatives, has been settled and parties have decided to give quietus to their dispute, I am of the opinion that the prayer made in the joint memo as well as in the petition is required to be granted.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER 1) Criminal Petition allowed;
2) The entire proceedings in C.C. No.8801 of 2022 pending before the VII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru arising out of Crime No.307 of 2021 Sri. Gowtham vs State Of Karnataka By on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45680696/
4 registered by Amruthahally Police Station, Bengaluru is quashed as against the petitioners.
